rounds.user: Let's init this new project. The idea is to build a smart harness that has a "map" UI element to keep track of the current topics/goals. It also support easy way to fork, checkpoint, and allow easy split of sessions, or even split from a previous checkpoint. The idea is that it makes it super easy for user to understand the sessions and switch contexts, where each point in a snapshot of context. So if you are writing a paper, you could first start with a linear line of sessions as you work on each sections. However, when you want to do some research you can fork or even go back and fork to explore a new angle without polluting the current contexts. You still keep the current context, but you now work on the new forked context. But all of these all easily visualized as a map, and when user click on the map nodes (with active sessions) you can jump to that session. We can even have a way to merge two sessions (we can discuss strategies later) but the idea for merging or spliting is that we can have LLM summerize the entire context window and then use it to spawn a new session with user's optional input on their goals to crete a hirarchy of priorities of goals. Let's work together to explore this idea. Use fable for this.

rounds.assistant: This is a sharper model than what we had, and it's worth slowing down for — because what you're describing quietly *unifies* three things we'd been treating as separate features. Let me lay out how I'd formalize it, then push back on two real problems. ## The reframe: delta nodes + composed contexts Your "every interaction creates incremental context" intuition maps onto a clean two-layer model: 1. **Delta node** — the new atomic unit. One turn = one delta: (user message + assistant response + tool calls/results), immutable, content-addressed. The graph stores *deltas*, not frozen whole-contexts. 2. **Context = a composition of deltas.** A "point" on the map stops being a mysterious snapshot and becomes something precise: an ordered list of delta references. The default composition is just your lineage prefix (`all deltas from root → here`). But nothing forces that. Once contexts are compositions, your whole feature list collapses into **one mechanism — editing the composition spec**: | Operation | Composition edit | |---|---| | **Rewind** | Drop the suffix: same branch, same goal, head moves back | | **Delete a turn** | Exclude one interior delta | | **Combine/import** | Include deltas from *other* branches | | **Sight** | Include a *distilled* stand-in for foreign deltas | | **Fork** | New branch (new goal) whose spec starts as a copy of a prefix | And yes — since each delta belongs to a branch, and each branch has a goal, **every delta is goal-labeled for free**. "Compose my current context + the findings from goal X" becomes a first-class, precise request. This is genuinely elegant, and I think it's the right data model. So: **doable — yes.** But two honest pushbacks: ## Pushback 1: conversation deltas are causally entangled — git's aren't This is the big one. In git, deleting a commit from the middle mostly works because file changes are near-independent. Conversation deltas are **not** independent: turn 13 was *generated conditioned on* turn 12. Delete turn 12 and: - Turn 13 may say "building on the function above" — now a dangling reference to nothing. - Turn 12's *information residue* survives in every later turn that absorbed it. You deleted the text, not the influence. - The resulting history is **counterfactual** — no agent ever actually experienced that conversation.
